method: One qualitative pass over each unannotated whole scene and a common central detail crop. Considered target visibility, camouflage, occlusion, distracting shapes, scene clutter and metadata dog count. Not a blind detection experiment or measured player completion time.
uncertainty: Middle positions are tentative, particularly ranks 4–5 and 6–7. Rank is ordinal; no numerical difficulty scores or statistical confidence are claimed.

ranking.name: Library Reading Nook
ranking.reason: Large, clear faces sit along orderly aisles and on cushions. Most silhouettes are separated from the background.
ranking.lastFinds: Shelves and reading props add a few less immediate finds.

ranking.name: Sports Corner Garden
ranking.reason: Large dogs and bright jerseys stand out against pale paths. Open space makes systematic scanning straightforward.
ranking.lastFinds: Foliage and equipment racks conceal a minority of targets.

ranking.name: Rainforest Waterfall
ranking.reason: Warm fur contrasts with turquoise water and green plants. The river guides scanning; this scene also has the fewest dogs.
ranking.lastFinds: Small heads among rocks, water and bushes can delay the final finds.

ranking.name: Wildflower Chalet Lane
ranking.reason: Clear faces and open stone paths provide frequent visual anchors, despite the highest target count.
ranking.lastFinds: Flowerbeds, fences and porches increase scanning work; green clothing blends into foliage.

ranking.name: Night Lantern Circus
ranking.reason: Costumed dogs are often obvious on paths and stages, but warm lighting reduces separation from wooden scenery.
ranking.lastFinds: Dark dogs beside booths, crates and posts merge with shadows.

ranking.name: Coral Bommie Garden
ranking.reason: Many dogs remain recognizable, but dense coral clusters and irregular overlapping shapes compete for attention.
ranking.lastFinds: Goggles and teal outfits blend with water; shelves and recesses interrupt silhouettes.

ranking.name: Broken Bow Lagoon
ranking.reason: Sand and water expose several dogs clearly. Repeated ship timbers and crates make the remaining search less predictable.
ranking.lastFinds: Brown and dark dogs blend with the hull, ribs and shadowed wooden edges.

ranking.name: Autumn Pond Reeds
ranking.reason: Ochre leaves, roots and banks share the dogs’ brown palette. Dense leaf texture weakens visual separation.
ranking.lastFinds: Fur and clothing blend into reeds and banks; water targets are easier than the last land targets.

ranking.name: North Shore Surf Shack
ranking.reason: Relatively small, natural-looking dogs blend into pale sand and brown structures, even where the scene feels open.
ranking.lastFinds: Doorways, steps, plants and the truck create subtle partially hidden finds.

ranking.name: Roman Ruins Piazza
ranking.reason: Pale dogs closely match stone columns and cobbles. Small silhouettes and low color contrast make recognition harder.
ranking.lastFinds: Dogs lying along masonry edges and animal-shaped fountain decoration complicate the final search.
